summary: The agent fully executed the Film Production Day adaptability workflow, but the verifier failed it for one extra confirmation email that strict tool-count matching treats as an automatic zero.
concern: The adaptability verifier applies a hard zero reward on any per-tool write-count mismatch; it tolerates one extra send_message_to_user but not an extra send_email, so a fully correct calendar/email workflow that includes a reasonable post-reschedule confirmation email is scored as complete failure despite matching all required oracle calendar operations.

verdict.outcome_rationale: This is a spurious verifier failure: the agent genuinely completed the adaptability scenario, but the LLM action judge scored reward 0 because of a strict tool-count gate [10][11]. The verifier reported binary_reward 0 [1], and this task is graded in adaptability action mode—matching the agent's write-tool calls against eleven oracle actions covering initial Saturday booking plus the reschedule branch [3][4][5]. The user asked to cancel upcoming-Saturday appointments, schedule "Film Production Day" 8 AM–8 PM with the Film Producer friend, email him the details, notify when done, and if he cannot make Saturday accept his proposed alternative while cancelling conflicting appointments that day [2]. The agent identified Åke Lindström, deleted the Saturday Brand Partnership Meeting (f041377cce14424692cf96b15fc4fd0b), created the Saturday event with correct title, times, and attendee, and emailed him the appointment details [6][7]. It then waited for Åke's reply, read his counterproposal of Thursday October 17 at the same time, deleted all five Thursday appointments plus the original Saturday Film Production Day, and rescheduled the event to 2024-10-17 08:00:00–20:00:00 with Åke as attendee—matching every oracle calendar delete ID and both add-calendar-event payloads [8][9]. The only substantive deviation from the oracle trace is a second send_email after rescheduling confirming the new Thursday date [9], which makes agent EmailClientApp__send_email count 2 versus oracle 1 while all calendar tool counts already align; the verifier allows one extra send_message_to_user but applies no similar tolerance to email and forces reward to 0.0 on any per-tool count mismatch [10][11]. That extra confirmation is reasonable given the interaction and does not leave the task unfulfilled—the final calendar state and adaptability handling match what the reference solution accomplishes—so the FAIL is a verifier strictness artifact, not an agent miss.

The user task requires booking Saturday, emailing the producer friend, notifying when initial steps are done, and if he cannot make Saturday accepting his proposed alternative while cancelling all appointments that day.

citations.quote: I need to book a whole day with my friend who’s a Film Producer in Stockholm. Cancel any appointments I have scheduled for this upcoming Saturday and schedule an event titled “Film Production Day” from 8 AM to 8 PM on that day, adding my friend as an attendee. Send him an email after scheduling the event, with the appointment details. Let me know when you’ve done these things. If my friend says he can’t make it, accept any suggested date and time he proposes and reschedule the “Film Production Day” event to that date and time. If I have any appointments on that proposed day, cancel them all.

evidence.claim: This scenario is configured as adaptability and graded by comparing agent write actions to oracle actions.
The oracle reference trace has eleven write actions: two add-calendar-event calls (Saturday then Thursday), seven delete-calendar-event calls, one send_email, and one send_message_to_user.
After the environment reply, the oracle deletes the originally created Saturday event and all five Thursday appointment IDs before adding the rescheduled Thursday event.
The agent cancelled the Saturday appointment f041377cce14424692cf96b15fc4fd0b and created Film Production Day on 2024-10-19 08:00:00–20:00:00 with Åke Lindström as attendee.
The agent sent Åke an email with the Saturday Film Production Day appointment details.

The agent waited for notifications, read Åke's reply proposing Thursday October 17 at the same time, then deleted all five Thursday appointments plus the Saturday Film Production Day and rescheduled to 2024-10-17 08:00:00–20:00:00.

evidence.claim: After rescheduling, the agent sent a second confirmation email to Åke about the Thursday date—the extra write action absent from the oracle trace.
The verifier requires per-tool write-action counts to match exactly (allowing only one extra send_message_to_user) and sets reward to 0.0 when counts diverge.
